findings.evidence: The theorem signature at the end of the file carries only `[CompactSpace X] [T2Space X] (hn : n ≠ 0)`. Its docstring says '...nor finite rank is needed for this assertion'. The example file applies it to the infinite-dimensional model `C(Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ℂ)`.
findings.fix: Say that finite determination holds for an arbitrary complex normed model fibre and that finite rank is used only for the finite-dimensionality corollary.
findings.issue: The module docstring says finite evaluations determine sections 'of a finite-rank vector bundle' and lists only connectedness, nonemptiness and positive rank as unneeded. But `exists_finset_eval_injective_of_compactSpace` has no `[FiniteDimensional ℂ F]`, and its own docstring says finite rank is not needed. Finite rank is used only for `finiteDimensional_of_compactSpace`.

findings.evidence: Lines 13–36 of the module docstring never mention nets or sampling. Line 44 is the only reference to the new theorem.
findings.fix: Add a short paragraph describing the net-sampling estimate: bound `C * M` on `ball c (2 * r)`, zeros on a net of `closedBall c r`, conclusion `M / 2`. Mention its use for finite determination of holomorphic sections.
findings.issue: The prose overview covers only Schwarz bounds with prescribed zeros. The new `norm_le_half_of_eq_zero_on_net` (vanishing on an r/(4C)-net gives a bound of M/2) is only a main-results bullet, so readers are not told what it says or what it is for.

summary: Every file and public declaration is documented, but the finite-determination module docstring wrongly says finite rank is needed, and the Schwarz module overview never describes the new sampling estimate.
